job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were helping their mother in the kitchen. Meera started washing the chopped spinach, but her mother stopped her. 'Always wash vegetables before cutting them,' she explained, 'otherwise, the vital nutrients wash away with the water.' Rohan asked if he should stop eating the butter on his roti because he wanted to stay fit. His mother smiled and said, 'Fats are essential for our body to function, provided we eat them in moderation, not in excess.' She then served them dal, explaining that proteins are body-building nutrients needed by everyone for growth and repair, not just bodybuilders. Later, they discussed why their grandmother took iron supplements. Rohan thought it was like eating metal nails, but his mother clarified that dietary iron is a mineral our body uses to stay healthy, not a hard metal. She reminded them that a balanced diet is not about eating equal amounts of everything, but eating the right proportion of nutrients based on what our body needs. Finally, she warned them that deficiency diseases like scurvy occur due to a lack of vitamins over time, not because of germs, so they cannot spread from person to person like a cold.

items.evidence: 'Always wash vegetables before cutting them,' she explained, 'otherwise, the vital nutrients wash away with the water.'
items.q: Why does Meera's mother want vegetables washed before they are chopped?
options: Cut pieces lose nutrients into the water
Cut pieces become cleaner and healthier
Cut pieces turn soft and spoil faster
Cut pieces soak up germs from water
items.explain: Washing after cutting lets vital nutrients dissolve and wash away with the water.

wrong.why: thinks washing after cutting makes veggies healthier
invents a spoilage reason not in the passage
reverses the effect of water on cut vegetables

items.evidence: His mother smiled and said, 'Fats are essential for our body to function, provided we eat them in moderation, not in excess.'
items.q: Rohan wants to stay fit. What should he do about the butter on his roti?
options: Eat a small amount of it
Remove it from his diet fully
Eat as much as he likes
Eat it only if it leaves marks
items.explain: Fats are essential for the body, but only in moderation, so a small amount is right.

wrong.why: mixes fats with the oily paper test

items.evidence: She then served them dal, explaining that proteins are body-building nutrients needed by everyone for growth and repair, not just bodybuilders.
items.q: Which person needs the protein in dal for growth and repair?
options: A child who never lifts weights
A wrestler who trains every day
A person trying to build big muscles
A person who plays sports often
items.explain: Proteins are needed by everyone for growth and repair, not only by people who build muscles.

items.q: Ravi has scurvy. Why is it safe to sit next to him?

It spreads only through a very loud cough
